title: AI Could Change Markets Forever - Systematic Investor - Ep.417

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/AI Could Change Markets Forever - Systematic Investor - Ep.417.docx

speakers: Niels Kastrup-Larsen (host, Top Traders Unplugged; caption spelling Neils Castro Razen)
Rob Carver (co-host, systematic trader and author)
summary: Top Traders Unplugged Ep.417 (Sept 2026): bond-market debt worries, the Simplify CTA ETF abandoning systematic discipline, and Rob Carver on fitting rule weights (average individual, asset-class and global fits) and limiting discretion to entries. Also AI risks in quant research, trend-following speed in V-shaped vs secular high-volatility regimes, and Man Group's quant-winter note.

completeness_estimate: 0.93 - first reader was thorough and accurate; missed Rob's view that Treasury buybacks are immaterial, the politics-vs-data point on asset-class fitting, and his reading of the paper's out-of-sample result

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: pumping up yields and making the life of uh central bankers quite difficult
claims.claim: Late summer 2026: worries over government and AI-complex corporate debt, and US fiscal promises, are pushing yields up.

claims.speaker: Niels Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: last week it proposed chopping the weight of government debt in its bond portfolio from 70 to 50%
claims.claim: Norway's sovereign wealth fund proposed cutting government debt from 70% to 50% of its bond portfolio (about 5% of its total, roughly $100bn), while the US Treasury expands long-end buybacks, e.g. 6bn in 10-20 year bonds.
claims.indicator: sovereign wealth fund bond allocation, Treasury buybacks

claims.speaker: Niels Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we know um from the CTA world that when you get big trends in bonds that's usually kind of an interesting uh time for for trend followers because it is a a big part of the overall portfolio
claims.claim: Big bond trends are good for trend followers; bonds drove returns in late 2021 to early 2023 and have detracted in the last two years, so a new bond trend could be coming.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I am short um US bonds, specifically 10 years
claims.claim: Rob's own positioning: short US 10-year and Korean 10-year bonds.

claims.speaker: Niels Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the manager so simplify basically stepped in and took some decisions based on on what you know exposure should be rather than following um the uh the signals
claims.claim: The Simplify managed futures ETF (ticker CTA) manager overrode subadvisor signals and removed the subadvisor, moving mainly to long energy, which investors in a systematic fund did not expect.

claims.speaker: Niels Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the underlying strategy can change, you know, in a heartbeat
claims.claim: ETF wrappers carry a risk that the strategy or the subadvisor changes without notice, unlike a fund run by the actual advisor.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: they've gone from um having over 50 markets, which is kind of, you know, an sort of reasonable amount of diversification
claims.claim: According to Seeking Alpha the ETF went from over 50 markets to energy only, losing diversification across many markets, which is why low-Sharpe strategies like trend following make money.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: investors are very concerned about style drift
claims.claim: Investors want diversified trend following and resist style drift, which limits research innovation at managers.

claims.speaker: Niels Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Millennium apparently is nearing hundred billion dollars under management
claims.claim: Millennium nearing $100bn AUM shows large allocations to multi-manager pods.

claims.speaker: Niels Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my trend barometer finished yesterday at 57
claims.claim: Trend barometer at 57 (strong), though equity momentum seems to be weakening after equities were a bright spot.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: where the market's kind of tottering on the edge of something, right?
claims.claim: Rob feels markets are poised for a shock without reacting, which means little trend profit; his risk is about a third of average and his year is about +7.5% mostly from early weeks.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: it is going to reach a crunch point where they can't release any more from there
claims.claim: The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve keeps falling and will hit a limit, a possible catalyst along with midterms and the new Fed chair.

claims.speaker: Niels Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the Btop 50 index is up 1.15% so far in September, up 12.42% so far this year
claims.claim: Mid-September 2026: BTOP50 +1.15% (YTD +12.42%), SG Trend about +12.1% YTD, versus MSCI World +12.78% and S&P 500 TR +12.45% YTD, world bonds -0.32% YTD.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG Trend, MSCI World, S&P 500 TR

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you probably shouldn't um fit everything individually because then you really do have a lot of noise and not much signal
claims.claim: Fitting rule weights per instrument is overfitting; fitting per asset class or pooled across all instruments does about as well.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: both did pretty well um and so um it's probably fine to do either of those
claims.claim: Pooled (all instruments) and asset-class fits both work; with few instruments (e.g. 2 bonds, 3 equities, 1 FX) do not fit by asset class.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I could just put a third of my risk capital in each and that's equivalent to just taking the average of those three
claims.claim: Most robust: average the individual, asset-class and global fits, which has about 0.98 to 0.99 correlation with global-only fitting, mattering more for small portfolios.

claims.speaker: Niels Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: use global parameter selection but then you have different models
claims.claim: Some managers use global parameters with different models for diversification.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I did look at that and found that it you know it makes things very complicated and it doesn't really add a lot of value
claims.claim: A matrix fit that allocates to fast trend in cheap, diversifying markets adds complexity but little value.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: my prior is to do no fitting yeah at all and only if I see strong evidence of add value will I do some fitting
claims.claim: Default to no fitting; fit only with strong, robust, out-of-sample evidence.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: they did agree that that yes all right systematic trading does actually mean literally blindly doing exactly what the system tells you
claims.claim: Systematic trading means following the system; overriding signals makes the system impossible to test.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: it makes it very hard to test um, whether your system's actually working or not
claims.claim: Ignoring system signals when inconvenient is the worst way to mix discretion and systematic.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: You have to be able to rank and order positions and and have sort of path dependent rules about swapping in and out positions
claims.claim: Non-leveraged traders must rank positions and use path-dependent swap rules.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: limit the discretionary part of a trading strategy to one tiny part, which is the what should I buy and when decision
claims.claim: Limit discretion to what and when to buy; make speed, exits and position size rule-based.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: 95% of retail traders lose money about 5% make money
claims.claim: 95% of retail traders lose money, mainly from position, cost and risk management errors, not entries alone.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: there are a lot of mutual fund managers with genuine skill at finding good stocks but actually terrible skill in choosing when to exit those positions
claims.claim: Skill in entries and in exits are separate; mutual fund managers pick well but exit poorly.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: essentially a statistically significant track record that proves that you have skill in doing that
claims.claim: Discretionary exits are allowed only with a statistically significant track record of skill.

claims.speaker: Niels Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I think where the big differentiator is between managers is actually how they manage the risk along the trade but also where they get out
claims.claim: Trend models enter at about the same time; managers differ in risk management and exit.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you should use a stop loss which is something I don't use myself of course
claims.claim: Where discretion is retained, use a simple stop-loss to hand exits to a rule.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the biggest debate um in the industry is over vol scaling after you after entry right
claims.claim: Biggest debate: whether to resize positions for volatility after entry or let them ride.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the biggest risk is potentially that it will just overfit um and you need to put very strong guard rails around it
claims.claim: AI in quant research mainly risks overfitting, needing guard rails and non-AI code.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I'd be really concerned if if people had you know live production code actually trading that that had been written by II with either no or or insufficient human oversight
claims.claim: AI code review found a serious bug but introduced a worse one that would have deleted all short positions, so AI-written code needs oversight.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: oversight governance and processes around code implementation are absolutely key
claims.claim: Governance and code oversight apply equally to AI-assisted systems.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: there will be quite a small percentage who are using AI correctly
claims.claim: A wave of consumer-grade AI trading may raise turnover, risk and volatility, but evidence is too early.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I think we're going to see a herd of uninformed AIdriven uh retail investors. Um, and uh, I think there'll be opportunities there.
claims.claim: Uninformed AI-driven retail herds create opportunities to trade the other side.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: it's been trained on reading the internet and you know on the internet there are lots of people saying including myself and you
claims.claim: LLMs recommend large trend-following allocations because their training text advocates it, so their advice is circular.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: 10 years is long enough normally to get some additional evidence
claims.claim: Revisit published research after about 10 years for out-of-sample evidence (Alpha Architect VIX and trend; Lasse Pedersen 100-year trend paper).

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: when the market's more volatile I I trade less momentum
claims.claim: Rob trades less momentum when volatility is high, while the article trades faster when VIX is high.

claims.speaker: Niels Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: being slow during periods like um the tariff tantrum whatever it was called liberation day
claims.claim: Slow trend following handled the tariff tantrum V-shape well, so being fast in high vol may not pay.
claims.indicator: slow vs fast trend in V-shape

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if the market is doing a Vshape, you want to be either very slow or very fast
claims.claim: In a V-shaped market be very fast or very slow, not medium speed; 2008 was a secular turn, not a V.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: slow trend following also very slow trend following also did well kind of medium speed would have done the worst
claims.claim: In COVID 2020 fast and slow trend followers did well and medium speed did worst, while in the 2025 tariff tantrum (very quick V) fast trend did worst.
claims.indicator: trend speed in COVID vs tariff tantrum

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: effectively high volatility could mean one of three different things
claims.claim: High volatility can mean 2008, 2020 or the tariff tantrum, with different optimal speeds, and one cannot know ahead which.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: when volatility is high trend following doesn't do as well is actually counterintuitive because people expect that high volatility is good for trend following
claims.claim: High volatility does not help trend following as the straddle intuition suggests, since results depend on trend speed, reaction speed and trading speed.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I have a prior towards simplicity which means I have a prior towards not doing this kind of thing
claims.claim: Rob will not implement VIX-based speed changes: prior toward simplicity, though the finding is not random data mining.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the quant winter was in it was 2018 to 2020 and and this was a period of time when these these factors did didn't do very well
claims.claim: Man Group note: classic factors (value, momentum) did badly in the 2018-2020 quant winter, and factor R-squared in manager returns varies over 25 years.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: quant equity quant managers are not all the same and they are doing things differently
claims.claim: Quant equity managers differ and do not simply hold basic factors.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: diversification has a habit of going away during events like the quant winter when everyone does
claims.claim: Diversification across managers disappears in crowded events like the quant winter.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if you can afford it you should you should definitely diversify because it's very hard to to pick who the best manager will be
claims.claim: Diversify across managers since picking the best is hard; quant equity offers rising idiosyncratic performance.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: 6 billion in in the US bond market is it's not even a drop in the ocean. It's like a drop a drop inside a drop in the ocean.
claims.claim: Treasury long-end buybacks of a few billion dollars are far too small to hold down US yields; at most they are a policy signal, and yields have kept rising despite them.
claims.indicator: Treasury buyback size vs market size
claims.direction: buybacks do not lower long yields
claims.testable: yes - yield reaction around buyback operations

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: that's actually um partly a political question in a way because um you know um as as people managing a specific part of our portfolio, we we you know we'd get very protective about it
claims.claim: Whether to use different rule weights (more carry, faster or slower trend) by asset class was partly decided by organisational politics in asset-class research teams; it should instead be treated as an empirical question tested on data.
claims.testable: yes - compare pooled vs asset-class fits out of sample

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: they they did find that it still this thing still seems to work.
claims.claim: Rob reads the decade-later Alpha Architect update as showing that VIX-dependent trend speed still seems to work out of sample, while warning that the headline result hides much and should not be copied into a system without understanding it.
